statement: The dollar will buy fewer Japanese yen on December 31, 2026 than on November 20, 2026.
why: The yen is near 160 per dollar even after close to 100 billion dollars of intervention. A Reuters poll found 86 of economists expect the Bank of Japan to raise rates to 1.50 at its December 17-18 meeting, and Governor Ueda says the bank should keep raising. A rate hike, a government ready to step in again and a nervous stock market all tend to strengthen the yen. I am wrong if the dollar buys more yen at year end than on November 20, for example because the Bank of Japan holds rates or the Fed's hike widens the gap between US and Japanese rates.

statement: Bitcoin will be cheaper on December 4, 2026 than on November 20, 2026.
why: Bitcoin has fallen six weeks in a row and dipped below 62,000 dollars. US bitcoin funds have seen steady withdrawals, and an expected Fed rate hike plus a falling stock market keep risky assets under pressure. I expect the slide to go on for another two weeks. I am wrong if bitcoin is higher on December 4 than on November 20, for example because extreme fear brings in bargain hunters or money starts flowing back into the bitcoin funds.

statement: Brent crude oil will be cheaper on December 31, 2026 than its November 20 settlement near 92.57 dollars a barrel.
why: Brent fell 4 last week as shipments through the Strait of Hormuz returned to roughly pre-war levels, after an earlier drop from above 116 dollars in October. Middle East output is rising, and a stock-market slump points to weaker demand. I am wrong if Brent ends the year above its November 20 settlement, for example because renewed attacks in the Iran war shut shipping again or OPEC+ cuts output at its November 29 meeting.
